simple.meaning: כָּלָא (kâlâʼ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to restrict , by act ( hold back or in ) or word ( prohibit ).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 18 times across Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, 1 Samuel, Psalms, and 6 more, beginning at Genesis 8:2. Its contexts include family line, offering, blood, commandment.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּלָא (H3607).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: כָּלָא (kâlâʼ) / H3607 is traced through Genesis 8:2, Genesis 23:6, Exodus 36:6, Numbers 11:28 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: The deep’s fountains and the sky’s windows were also stopped, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
“Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the best of our tombs. None of us will withhold from you his tomb. Bury your dead.”

Moses gave a commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, “Let neither man nor woman make anything else for the offering for the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing.
Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his chosen men, answered, “My lord Moses, forbid them!”
The men did so, and took two milk cows and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home.
Blessed is your discretion, and blessed are you, who have kept me today from blood guiltiness, and from avenging myself with my own hand.
I have not hidden your righteousness within my heart.
For innumerable evils have surrounded me.
My eyes are dim from grief.
I have kept my feet from every evil way,

There is no man who has power over the spirit to contain the spirit; neither does he have power over the day of death. There is no discharge in war; neither shall wickedness deliver those who practice it.
I will tell the north, ‘Give them up!’
Now at that time the king of Babylon’s army was besieging Jerusalem. Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard, which was in the king of Judah’s house.
For Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, “Why do you prophesy, and say, ‘Yahweh says, “Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will take it;

“The Lord Yahweh says: ‘In the day when he went down to Sheol * Sheol is the place of the dead. I caused a mourning. I covered the deep for him, and I restrained its rivers. The great waters were stopped. I caused Lebanon to mourn for him, and all the trees of the field fainted for him.

“Seventy weeks are decreed on your people and on your holy city, to finish disobedience, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most holy.
Therefore for your sake the heavens withhold the dew, and the earth withholds its fruit.
Therefore for your sake the heavens withhold the dew, and the earth withholds its fruit.

definitions.short: to restrict , by act ( hold back or in ) or word ( prohibit )
definitions.usage: finish, forbid, keep (back), refrain, restrain, retain, shut up, be stayed, withhold.
definitions.full: H3607. kala [ כָּלָא ] verb shut up, restrain, withhold (Late Hebrew id. ; Aramaic כְּלָא , ; Ethiopic restrain, hinder ; Assyrian Kâlû, id.; Arabic protect Qor 21:43 compare Ba ZMG 1887, 605 Anm. 4 ) — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular suffix כְּלָאוֺ Jer 32:3 ; 3 feminine singular כָּֽלְאָה Hag 1:10 ; 2 feminine singular suffix כְּלִתִ֫נִי 1Sam 25:33 ; 1 singular כָּלִאתִי Psa 119:101 ; 3 plural כָּֽלְאוּ Hag 1:10 , כָּלוּ 1Sam 6:10 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִכְלֶה Gen 23:6 ; 2 masculine singular תִּכְלָא Psa 40:12 ; 2 feminine singular תִּכְלָאִ֑י Isa 43:6 ; 1 singular אֶכְלָא Psa 40:10 ; Imperative suffix כְּלָאֵם Num 11:28 ; Infinitive construct לִכְלוֺא Eccl 8:8 ; Passive participle כָּלוּא Jer 32:2 , כָּלֻא Psa 88:9 ; (on the metaplastic forms, as if from כלה , see Ges § 75 , 21 c Kö i. 611 ); — 1 shut up , with accusative 1Sam 6:10 (+ בְ local), Jer 32:3 ; passive participle 32:2 ( בְ local), figurative Psa 88:9 (opposed to יצא ). 2 restrain , with accusative 1Sam 25:33 (+ בְדָמִים מִבּוֺא ), Psa 119:101 (+ מִכָּלֿ ); כְּלָאֵם (sc. מֵהִתְנַבֵּא ) Num 11:28 ; ׳כ שְׂפָתַי Psa 40:10 ; ׳כ אֶתהָֿרוּחַ Eccl 8:8 . On Psa 74:11 see כלה Pi`el 2. 3. withhold , מֵתֶ֑ךָ מִקְּבֹר מִמְּךָ ׳כ אֶתקִֿבְרוֺ Gen 23:6 (P), ׳כ מִמֶּ֑נּי רַחֲמֶיךָ Psa 40:12 ; Hag 1:10 b, probably also v a (read טָ֑ל for מִטָּ֑ל ᵐ5 ᵑ0 , We); absolute אַלתִּֿכְלָאִי (that is, exiles) Isa 43:6 (|| תְּנִי ). Niph`al Imperfect מִןהַֿשָּׁמַיִם הַגֶּשֶׁם וַיִּכָּלֵא Gen 8:2 (J), and the rain from heaven was restrained , compare רַבִּים מַיִם וַיִּכָּֽלְאוּ Ezek 31:15 (in figurative; || מנע ); מֵהָבִיא הָעָם וַיִּכָּלֵא Exod 36:6 (P). Pi`el [Perfect כִּלָּא and] Infinitive construct לְכַלֵּא see כלה Pi`el
